info.title: OpenVibe.Codes API
info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.Codes as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.380.0): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. Generated by openvibe-contracts lib/openapi.js; do not edit.

get.summary: Read one person's Action Center items from OpenVibe.Codes (plan 2026-10-28 §3.10): coding tasks run through OpenVibe.Run (queued, placed, running, done, failed), as common.action-list-result@1.
get.description: **codes.actions.read** (first-party): Read one person's Action Center items from OpenVibe.Codes (plan 2026-10-28 §3.10): coding tasks run through OpenVibe.Run (queued, placed, running, done, failed), as common.action-list-result@1. GET /api/v1/actions?subject=usr_… with a service token; granted to OpenVibe.Network's aggregator only. Never another person's items, and only the fields of common.action-item@1.

post.summary: Start a coding task for a person on their own machine: POST /api/v1/tasks on OpenVibe.Codes, as a first-party service naming the person in X-OV-Subject (OpenVibe.Actor routes coding work here, plan T1
post.description: **codes.task.start** (first-party): Start a coding task for a person on their own machine: POST /api/v1/tasks on OpenVibe.Codes, as a first-party service naming the person in X-OV-Subject (OpenVibe.Actor routes coding work here, plan T17). Codes submits it to OpenVibe.Run as that person, in the project of their latest openvibe.codes/run task, and Run places it only on a machine of theirs (platform.resource-offer@1 owner). The person pays nothing to OpenVibe for it: the model use is on their own machine's keys.

get.summary: Read a coding task started through codes.task.start: GET /api/v1/tasks/:id on OpenVibe.Codes, as the service that started it, naming the same person in X-OV-Subject.
get.description: **codes.task.read** (first-party): Read a coding task started through codes.task.start: GET /api/v1/tasks/:id on OpenVibe.Codes, as the service that started it, naming the same person in X-OV-Subject. Another service's task, or another person's, is 404. The answer is codes.task@2: the task itself (as codes.task@1, with the same fields at the top level) and, added to it, the task's attempts (its timeline) and its outcome.

post.summary: Cancel a coding task started through codes.task.start that has not ended: POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/cancel on OpenVibe.Codes, as the service that started it, naming the same person in X-OV-Subject.
post.description: **codes.task.cancel** (first-party): Cancel a coding task started through codes.task.start that has not ended: POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/cancel on OpenVibe.Codes, as the service that started it, naming the same person in X-OV-Subject. Codes cancels the Run job; the task ends cancelled (an ended one is answered as it is).

get.summary: Manage the configuration namespaces and secrets of OpenVibe.Codes through openvibe-shared/config (D11): GET /internal/config lists the namespace summaries, GET /internal/config/:namespace returns one
get.description: **codes.config.manage** (internal): Manage the configuration namespaces and secrets of OpenVibe.Codes through openvibe-shared/config (D11): GET /internal/config lists the namespace summaries, GET /internal/config/:namespace returns one as common.config-namespace@1, POST applies common.config-change@1, and PUT /internal/config/:namespace/secrets/:key sets a secret with common.config-secret-put@1 (write-only; the answer is the marker) while DELETE removes it. POST /internal/config/:namespace/test/:key asks the service's tester to try a stored value with the provider on the server, answering { ok, message } in one line that never carries a secret (the owner's Setup tab). Only Network's admin proxy, acting for the owner, holds this capability; it is never grantable to apps. Each request carries the owner as actor, and the service audits every write with that actor and key, never a secret value.

ai.run-error.v1.title: AiRunError
ai.run-error.v1.description: ai.run-error@1: safe, actionable words for an AI or Actor run. Raw provider responses are never display text. The code map is shared across products.

codes.task-start-request.v1.title: CodesTaskStartRequest
codes.task-start-request.v1.description: codes.task-start-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/tasks on OpenVibe.Codes (capability codes.task.start). A first-party service (OpenVibe.Actor) starts a coding task for a person, named with X-OV-Subject: Codes runs it on that person's own machine through OpenVibe.Run (openvibe.codes/run, plan T16), in the project of their latest task there, so the person has used openvibe.codes/run once before a service can start one for them (else 409 codes.no_project). REPO is an https git URL with no credentials; REF a branch or tag to start from (default: the repository's default branch). PROMPT is the task. AGENT names one of Codes' agents (GET /harnesses), absent for Codes' router to pick. PERMISSION: review (read-only: research, audits, reviews; nothing is changed), edit (default; the agents edit files) or full (they may also run commands: tests, installs). PUSH asks for the change on a new branch (GitHub, with the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN; never the branch it started from), PULL_REQUEST also opens a pull request. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat for the same person with the same key answers the first task (200, created false).

actor_task_id.description: The OpenVibe.Actor task id when this coding task was started from Actor.

actor_step_id.description: The OpenVibe.Actor step id when this coding task was started from Actor.

codes.task-start-result.v1.title: CodesTaskStartResult
codes.task-start-result.v1.description: codes.task-start-result@1: the answer of POST /api/v1/tasks (201 created, or 200 with created false for a repeated idempotency key).

codes.task.v1.title: CodesTask
codes.task.v1.description: codes.task@1: a coding task on OpenVibe.Codes, as GET /api/v1/tasks/:id answers it (capability codes.task.read) and POST /api/v1/tasks creates it. STATE follows the OpenVibe.Run job that carries it: queued (waiting for one of the person's machines), placed, running, then succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired (no machine of theirs took it in time). URL is the task's page on openvibe.codes, where its owner follows it live. RESULT is present once it has ended: OK says whether the agents finished, SUMMARY what they said, FILES and PATCH the change (the patch at most 256 KiB, PATCH_TRUNCATED when cut), PUSH where it went when asked, COST_USD the model use on the person's own keys, DURATION_MS the time on their machine. ERROR says why a task that never ran ended (Run refused it, or the job failed before a result).

actor_ref.description: The OpenVibe.Actor task and step that started this coding task, when it came from Actor.

codes.task.v2.title: CodesTask
codes.task.v2.description: codes.task@2: a coding task on OpenVibe.Codes, as GET /api/v1/tasks/:id answers it (capability codes.task.read) and POST /api/v1/tasks creates it. It is codes.task@1 with two added fields: ATTEMPTS, the task's timeline (each try of the task, with the state it ended in and why), and OUTCOME, what the task's attempts added up to (done, unfinished with what is left, or stopped). STATE follows the OpenVibe.Run job that carries it: queued (waiting for one of the person's machines), placed, running, then succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired (no machine of theirs took it in time). URL is the task's page on openvibe.codes, where its owner follows it live. RESULT is present once it has ended: OK says whether the agents finished, SUMMARY what they said, FILES and PATCH the change (the patch at most 256 KiB, PATCH_TRUNCATED when cut), PUSH where it went when asked, COST_USD the model use on the person's own keys, DURATION_MS the time on their machine. ERROR says why a task that never ran ended (Run refused it, or the job failed before a result).

actor_ref.description: The OpenVibe.Actor task and step that started this coding task, when it came from Actor.

attempts.description: The task's timeline: every try of it, in order. The first is the task itself; the others are what the agents did after it (the same conversation carried on, another agent taking over, a last turn before a limit).

n.description: The attempt's number, 1 for the first try.

machine.description: The node that ran the attempt, or sandbox when it ran in a sandbox.

session.description: The harness session, so a following attempt can carry on in the same conversation.

why.description: One plain sentence: why this attempt happened, or how it ended.

end_why.description: How the attempt ended, in plain words.

outcome.description: What the task's attempts added up to: done, unfinished (with what is left), or stopped. Null while the task still runs.

common.action-item.v1.title: ActionItem
common.action-item.v1.description: One piece of a person's agent work in the Action Center (plan 2026-10-28 §3.10): an agent task, a coding task, an AI run, or an approval waiting on them. Each authority answers its own items in this shape (common.action-list-result@1); OpenVibe.Network merges them into buckets (network.me-actions-result@1). Text is plain (no markup); a cost is what the person was charged in USD, null when unknown or free; href is a page on the authority's own public site.

service.description: The authority that owns the item.

id.description: The authority's own id (tsk_…, a Codes task id, run_…, a confirmation id, dpr_…).

title.description: A short plain-text name: the start of the task text, the workflow, or what the approval is for.

summary.description: The last step, the outcome, or what will happen on approval.

bucket.description: Where the Action Center shows it: running (queued or working), waiting (needs the person), scheduled (will run later), done, failed (failed, cancelled or expired).

state.description: The authority's own state word (queued, running, needs_you, succeeded, failed, cancelled, pending…).

agent.description: The agent, model or workflow doing it, when known.

cost_usd.description: What it cost the person, in US dollars; null when unknown or free.

steps.description: Tool calls or steps so far, when counted.

error.description: Why it failed, in words a person can act on.

next_run_at.description: When a scheduled item runs next.

href.description: The item's page: its live steps, receipt or approval.

actions.description: What the person can do from the list. approve/decline/cancel/retry go through OpenVibe.Network (POST /api/v1/me/actions/:service/:id/:action); open is a link.

skill.description: Catalogue skill key, when this run came from a skill.

subject.description: The content this run is about, with its canonical page when known.

run_error.description: Safe error words and the next useful action. Never a raw provider response.

step.description: The latest live step in plain words.

common.action-list-result.v1.title: ActionListResult
common.action-list-result.v1.description: One authority's Action Center items for a person (capabilities actor.actions.read, codes.actions.read, ai.actions.read, domains.actions.read): GET /api/v1/actions?subject=usr_… with the caller's service token. Everything running, waiting or scheduled, then done and failed items from the last 30 days, newest first, at most 50.

common.config-change.v1.title: ConfigChange
common.config-change.v1.description: common.config-change@1 (AI Exchange D11): body of POST /internal/config/:namespace on a service's openvibe-shared/config admin routes. It proposes a new revision of the namespace and activates it (the store validates against the namespace schema, applies env pins and calls onActivate). `merge: true` starts from the active values; otherwise `values` is the whole new set. `unset` removes keys. A secret-class key's value is never sent here: it is 422 config.secret_write_only; use common.config-secret-put@1.

values.description: The new values, one member per key. The store validates them against the namespace schema; a secret-class value here is refused.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value; a redaction marker keeps the value it stands for.

reason.description: Why the change is made; it is the revision's reason in the history.

merge.description: Merge into the active values instead of replacing them.

unset.description: Keys to remove from the new revision.

common.config-namespace.v1.title: ConfigNamespace
common.config-namespace.v1.description: common.config-namespace@1 (AI Exchange D11): one service configuration namespace as openvibe-shared/config's summary() returns it (config-pg.js), plus `sealed`, `pins` and `schema`. GET /internal/config lists these for a service and GET /internal/config/:namespace returns one. Values are the active ones over the defaults, with every secret-class value replaced by its marker; a marker never carries the value. `sealed` says whether the service has a KEK so secrets are envelopes (false is the pre-D11 plaintext behaviour). `pins` names the keys whose x-env variable is set, so their effective value is the environment's and a write is 409 config.pinned_in_env. `schema` is the namespace's JSON Schema so a client can draw the form; its annotations are title, description, x-group, x-env, x-danger, x-bind and x-unit (nano_usd, ms, bps, seconds), and for the owner's Setup tab and the clear admin panel (openvibe-shared 4.125.0) x-owner-input ({ group, unlocks, get_it_at, get_it_how, test }: a field only the owner can give), x-required-for (the feature an unset field blocks), x-enum-labels ({ value: { label, description } }), x-advanced (folded under Advanced settings) and x-example (a placeholder; never on a secret).

revision.description: The active revision; null before the namespace has one.

values.description: The active values over the defaults, one member per key. A secret-class key's value is a marker, never the value.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value. An object with a redacted member is a secret marker, and nothing else.

classification.description: Every key of values, classified. A key the service does not classify is internal.

sealed.description: True when the service has a KEK: secret-class values are stored as envelopes and only opened for a caller that needs them. False keeps the pre-D11 plaintext-inside-values_json behaviour, and the tab shows it in red.

pins.description: The keys whose x-env variable is set in the service process: their effective value is the environment's, read-only, and a write answers 409 config.pinned_in_env.

schema.description: The namespace's JSON Schema, or null when it has none. Annotations the client may read: title, description, x-group, x-env, x-danger, x-bind (the key whose value the secret is bound to), x-unit (nano_usd, ms, bps or seconds), x-owner-input, x-required-for, x-enum-labels, x-advanced and x-example.

active.description: The active revision as a snapshot (common.config-snapshot@1), or null.

last_known_good.description: The last revision that activated cleanly (common.config-snapshot@1), or null.

marker.description: A secret-class value, as the summary and the secret endpoints show it: never the value. The fingerprint is keyed, so equal fingerprints within one namespace mean the value did not change.

fingerprint.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the value, keyed with the namespace's secret key.

hint.description: The four-character hint (the value's last four characters), never more.

bound_to.description: The value of the key named by x-bind when the secret was set, e.g. a provider base_url origin.

common.config-snapshot.v1.title: ConfigSnapshot
common.config-snapshot.v1.description: One immutable revision of one service's configuration namespace (roadmap WS-C task 7; kept by openvibe-shared/config). A revision's values never change: revisions grow by one per namespace, and a rollback is a new revision that copies an older one's values. Only the state moves: proposed -> active -> superseded or rolled_back, or proposed -> rejected when validation or activation fails, in which case the previous active revision stays or is restored. A secret-class key's value never appears here: it is { redacted: true, fingerprint }, an HMAC-SHA256 of the value under a secret key the service keeps per namespace, so equal fingerprints within one namespace mean the value did not change, while the value cannot be recovered or guessed offline without that key. checksum is the sha256 of the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace) of values exactly as they appear here, secrets as their markers, so anyone can check it, and two snapshots of one namespace with the same checksum hold the same configuration.

previous_revision.description: The revision that was active when this one was proposed; null for the namespace's first.

values.description: The configuration, one member per key. A secret-class key's value is a redaction marker.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value. An object with a redacted member is a redaction marker, and nothing else.

fingerprint.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the value, keyed with the namespace's secret key: equal within one namespace when the value is unchanged, and not recoverable or guessable without the key.

classification.description: Every key of values, classified. A key the service does not classify is internal.

checksum.description: sha256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of values as they appear in this snapshot (secrets as their markers).

activated_at.description: When it became active; null while proposed, and for a rejected revision.

error.description: Why it was rejected: the validation errors, or what activation reported. Never a secret value.

copied_from.description: A rollback's source: the revision whose values this one copies.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
